frames.title: Market Sophistication Lesson

Market Sophistication Lesson
What your consumers see

Lesson
These shirts represent what your potential customers see in the market.
When all of the shirts look the same, there is no clear or obvious choice... They all seem to be the same, so you just pick one.
But when a well branded OR a new mechanism/product is introduced, it automatically grabs attention and becomes the more attractive choice in the market

frames.title: What Is Market Sophistication Diagram and Levels
frames.on_screen:
What Is Market Sophistication
Understanding how many products & solutions have been presented to that level of market awareness before
Market sophistication is the level of knowledge your market has on your products/services.
How many similar products has your market been told about before?
And how many similar products have they tried?

Chart:
Y-axis: Level of Market Sophistication
X-axis: Time, Amount and Quality of Buying Experiences
Trend arrow pointing up-right: Increasing Skepticism

Levels:
- Level 1: Brand New Market - Make any claim
- Level 2: Make a Bigger Claim than your Competitor
- Level 3: Introduce a Big Differentiator that supports the Claim and Convinces the Mind
- Level 4: Create a newer or better Differentiator, or improve on the previous one. "Widget 2.0"
- Level 5: Differentiator burns out. Audience skepticism is at an all time high. Full-on Empathic Marketing is now the only option.
[Attributed note in small font at bottom right]: Adapted from Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising

frames.title: Market Sophistication - Stage #1
frames.on_screen:
Market Sophistication - Stage #1
State the claim

Definition:
First to market aka the Market Has Never Seen your product.
Goal:
Be Simple, Be Direct.
Action:
Name the claim & prove it works.

BlackBerry visual:
[BlackBerry pager ad mock-up with image and text:] "In 1999, RIM released their first Blackberry, a two-way pager that could receive email, and named it after it's keyboard's likeness to the fruit"
frames.not_in_transcript: Text on image: "In 1999, RIM released their first Blackberry, a two-way pager that could receive email, and named it after it's keyboard's likeness to the fruit"

frames.title: Market Sophistication - Stage #2
frames.on_screen:
Market Sophistication - Stage #2
Enlarge The Claim

Definition:
Market Is Starting To See It
Goal:
Enlarge the successful claim of competitors & one-up your competitors.
Action:
Make bigger & stronger claims.

[Visual: Nokia E62 advertisement image with slogan 'NOKIA Connecting People']

frames.title: Market Sophistication - Stage #3
frames.on_screen:
Market Sophistication - Stage #3
Provide a New Mechanism (how to achieve the claim)

Definition:
Market Has Heard All The Claims
Goal:
Introduce a new mechanism
Action:
Focus on HOW the product delivers the SAME claim in a NEW & better way

[Visual: Original Apple iPhone ad showing hand touching the screen; text: "Touching is believing. The revolutionary new iPhone is now available at Apple and AT&T retail stores."]
frames.not_in_transcript: iPhone ad text: "Touching is believing. The revolutionary new iPhone is now available at Apple and AT&T retail stores."

frames.title: Market Sophistication - Stage #4
frames.on_screen:
Market Sophistication - Stage #4
Enlarge the Mechanism (Stage #2 applied to mechanism)

Definition:
Market Now Knows The Mechanisms
Goal:
Enlarging your mechanism.
Action:
Make it easier, faster, solve it better, overcome limitations.

[Visual: iPhone 3G ad showing front and profile; text: 'iPhone 3G', 'Twice as fast.', 'Half the price.']

frames.title: Market Sophistication - Stage #5
frames.on_screen:
Market Sophistication - Stage #5
Identification

Definition:
Market No Longer Believes You
Goal:
Focus your advertising on identification with your prospect.
Action:
Show the market the version of themselves they want to become, selling the persona of using your product.

[Two video thumbnails: top showing Rolex mountain commercial, bottom showing Nike 'Find Your Greatness' jogger commercial]

frames.title: How To Determine Market Sophistication
frames.on_screen:
How To Determine Market Sophistication
how many products or solutions have your consumers seen before

1. Analyze your product & the problems it solves
2. Identify all of the competitors selling the same product
3. Identify all of the business solving the same problem

Key Point: You will experience market sophistication as you do research. One of the main goals of research, is to identify market sophistication & be in the seat of your potential customer.
